subproblem.title: The ball integral x ↦ ∫_{B_r(x) × G(N,n)} β(S) dν is Borel
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, let G(N,n) = Grassmannian N n (projection matrices with the subspace topology and Borel σ-algebra), and let ν be an s-finite measure on ℝ^N × G(N,n) (product σ-algebra). Then for every r ∈ ℝ and every continuous β : G(N,n) → ℝ, the map ℝ^N → ℝ, x ↦ ∫_{B_r(x) × G(N,n)} β(S) dν(y, S), is Borel measurable. Here B_r(x) = closedBall x r and the integral is the Bochner set integral, which is 0 when the integrand is not ν-integrable on B_r(x) × G(N,n).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclidean N × Grassmannian N n)), SFinite ν → ∀ (r : ℝ) (β : C(Grassmannian N n, ℝ)), Measurable (fun x : Euclidean N ↦ ∫ z in closedBall x r ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)), β z.2 ∂ν)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 3 of the parent-supplied proof of frt_vgm_measurable_plane_selection (part of the Borel version of x ↦ T_x needed in Simon, Ch. 8, proof of 1.2, p. 208). There it is applied to ν = V.measure, which is σ-finite (Varifold.measure.instSigmaFinite) and hence s-finite; here it is stated for an arbitrary s-finite ν on ℝ^N × G(N,n).

Let N, n ∈ ℕ, let ν be an s-finite measure on ℝ^N × G, G := Grassmannian N n, and fix r ∈ ℝ and β ∈ C(G, ℝ).

1. Let E_r := {p ∈ ℝ^N × (ℝ^N × G) : dist p.2.1 p.1 ≤ r}. The map p ↦ dist p.2.1 p.1 is continuous (Continuous.dist of continuous_fst ∘ continuous_snd and continuous_fst), so E_r is closed (isClosed_le with the constant r).

2. ℝ^N is second countable with its Borel σ-algebra, and G is second countable (Grassmannian.instSecondCountableTopology) with the subtype σ-algebra, which is its Borel σ-algebra. Hence the product σ-algebra on ℝ^N × (ℝ^N × G) contains every open set (OpensMeasurableSpace of products of second-countable spaces), and the closed set E_r is measurable (IsClosed.measurableSet).

3. Define F : ℝ^N × (ℝ^N × G) → ℝ by F := E_r.indicator (p ↦ β(p.2.2)). The map p ↦ p.2.2 is measurable (measurable_snd twice) and β is continuous, hence measurable (β.continuous.measurable); so p ↦ β(p.2.2) is measurable and, E_r being measurable, its indicator F is measurable (Measurable.indicator). A measurable real-valued function is strongly measurable (Measurable.stronglyMeasurable; ℝ is second countable and metrizable).

4. ν is s-finite, so MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable.integral_prod_right', applied to F and ν, shows that x ↦ ∫ F(x, z) dν(z) is strongly measurable, hence measurable (StronglyMeasurable.measurable).

5. Fix x ∈ ℝ^N. The set closedBall x r ×ˢ univ is measurable (measurableSet_closedBall.prod MeasurableSet.univ), so integral_indicator (which needs no integrability) gives ∫_{closedBall x r ×ˢ univ} β(z.2) dν(z) = ∫ (closedBall x r ×ˢ univ).indicator (z ↦ β z.2) z dν(z). For every z ∈ ℝ^N × G, z ∈ closedBall x r ×ˢ univ ⇔ dist z.1 x ≤ r ⇔ (x, z) ∈ E_r (Set.mem_prod, Metric.mem_closedBall, Set.mem_univ). So the two integrands agree pointwise: (closedBall x r ×ˢ univ).indicator (z ↦ β z.2) z = F(x, z).

6. By Step 5 (function extensionality in x), the map in the statement equals x ↦ ∫ F(x, z) dν(z), which is measurable by Step 4. ∎
proof_key_steps: E_r = {(x, z) : dist z.1 x ≤ r} is closed in ℝ^N × (ℝ^N × G), hence measurable (second-countable factors).
F := 1_{E_r}(x, z) β(z.2) is measurable, hence strongly measurable.
ν is s-finite, so StronglyMeasurable.integral_prod_right' makes x ↦ ∫ F(x, z) dν(z) measurable.
integral_indicator and the pointwise identity 1_{B_r(x)×G}(z) β(z.2) = F(x, z) identify the ball integral with ∫ F(x, ·) dν.

audit.reason: The type exactly matches the stated Bochner set integral for arbitrary s-finite ν. The jointly measurable indicator is strongly measurable, and integral_prod_right' supplies parameter measurability without an integrability premise. integral_indicator and the verified slice identity yield the exact conclusion, including empty Grassmannians and nonintegrable integrands. The proof is complete and independent.

subproblem.title: A measurable G(N,n)-valued selection of entrywise limits of measurable matrix sequences
subproblem.statement: Let X be a measurable space and N, n ∈ ℕ with G(N,n) = Grassmannian N n nonempty (G(N,n) is the subtype of real N × N matrices P with P symmetric, P P = P and trace P = n, with the induced σ-algebra). Let a : ℕ → X → (Fin N → Fin N → ℝ) be such that every entry map x ↦ a_k(x)_{ij} is measurable (k ∈ ℕ, i, j ∈ Fin N). Then there is a measurable τ : X → G(N,n) such that for every x ∈ X and T ∈ G(N,n): if a_k(x)_{ij} → T_{ij} as k → ∞ for all i, j, then τ(x) = T.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [MeasurableSpace X] (N n : ℕ), Nonempty (Grassmannian N n) → ∀ (a : ℕ → X → Fin N → Fin N → ℝ), (∀ (k : ℕ) (i j : Fin N), Measurable (fun x ↦ a k x i j)) → ∃ τ : X → Grassmannian N n, Measurable τ ∧ ∀ (x : X) (T : Grassmannian N n), (∀ i j : Fin N, Tendsto (fun k ↦ a k x i j) atTop (𝓝 (T.1 i j))) → τ x = T
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 5–6 and the identification in Step 7 of the parent-supplied proof of frt_vgm_measurable_plane_selection (the Borel version T̃ of x ↦ T_x needed in Simon, Ch. 8, proof of 1.2, p. 208). There X = ℝ^N and a_k(x)_{ij} is the ball average of the matrix entry S ↦ S_{ij} at radius 1/(k+1); here the sequence is arbitrary.

Notation: 𝒢 := {P ∈ Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℝ : P.IsSymm ∧ P * P = P ∧ P.trace = n}, so G(N,n) = {P // P ∈ 𝒢} with the subtype σ-algebra. The matrix space carries the product (Pi) σ-algebra, which is its Borel σ-algebra because Fin N is countable and ℝ is second countable and Borel (Matrix BorelSpace instance). 𝒢 is closed (Grassmannian.isClosed_projectionSet), hence measurable (IsClosed.measurableSet). Decidability of set membership is classical.

1. Since G(N,n) is nonempty, fix S₀ ∈ G(N,n); then S₀.1 ∈ 𝒢 (S₀.2).

2. Convergence sets. For i, j ∈ Fin N put C^{ij} := {x ∈ X : ∃ c ∈ ℝ, Tendsto (k ↦ a_k(x)_{ij}) atTop (𝓝 c)}. Each x ↦ a_k(x)_{ij} is measurable and ℝ is completely metrizable, second countable and Borel, so C^{ij} is measurable (MeasureTheory.measurableSet_exists_tendsto, with the countably generated filter atTop on ℕ).

3. Limits. Put L^{ij}(x) := limUnder atTop (k ↦ a_k(x)_{ij}) ∈ ℝ. Each x ↦ a_k(x)_{ij} is a measurable real function, hence strongly measurable (Measurable.stronglyMeasurable). ℝ is nonempty and completely metrizable, so MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable.limUnder shows that L^{ij} is strongly measurable, hence measurable.

4. Limit matrix. Let M(x) := Matrix.of (fun i j ↦ L^{ij}(x)). Every entry x ↦ M(x)_{ij} = L^{ij}(x) is measurable, so M : X → Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℝ is measurable (Measurable.of_eval_matrix).

5. Good set. Let Y := (⋂_{i} ⋂_{j} C^{ij}) ∩ M⁻¹(𝒢). It is measurable: a finite intersection of the measurable sets of Step 2 (MeasurableSet.iInter twice), intersected with the preimage of the measurable set 𝒢 under the measurable map M.

6. Definition of τ. Let M' := Y.piecewise M (fun _ ↦ S₀.1), i.e. M'(x) = M(x) for x ∈ Y and M'(x) = S₀.1 otherwise. M' is measurable (Measurable.piecewise: Y is measurable, M is measurable, constants are measurable). For every x, M'(x) ∈ 𝒢: if x ∈ Y, then M'(x) = M(x) ∈ 𝒢 by the second component of the definition of Y (Set.piecewise_eq_of_mem); if x ∉ Y, then M'(x) = S₀.1 ∈ 𝒢 (Set.piecewise_eq_of_notMem, Step 1). Define τ(x) := ⟨M'(x), M'(x) ∈ 𝒢⟩ ∈ G(N,n). τ is measurable (Measurable.subtype_mk applied to the measurable M').

7. The selection property. Let x ∈ X and T ∈ G(N,n) with Tendsto (k ↦ a_k(x)_{ij}) atTop (𝓝 (T.1 i j)) for all i, j. Since atTop on ℕ is a nontrivial filter and ℝ is Hausdorff, Tendsto.limUnder_eq gives L^{ij}(x) = T.1 i j for all i, j, hence M(x) = T.1 (Matrix.ext / extensionality in i, j). Moreover x ∈ C^{ij} for all i, j (witness c = T.1 i j) and M(x) = T.1 ∈ 𝒢 (T.2), so x ∈ Y. Therefore M'(x) = M(x) = T.1 (Set.piecewise_eq_of_mem), i.e. the underlying matrices of τ(x) and T agree, and τ(x) = T by Subtype.ext. ∎
proof_key_steps: Fix S₀ ∈ G(N,n); 𝒢 is closed, hence measurable in the Borel matrix space.
Convergence sets C^{ij} are measurable (measurableSet_exists_tendsto) and limits L^{ij} = limUnder are measurable (StronglyMeasurable.limUnder).
M(x) := Matrix.of (L^{ij}(x)) is measurable (Measurable.of_eval_matrix); Y := ⋂ C^{ij} ∩ M⁻¹(𝒢) is measurable.
τ := ⟨Y.piecewise M (const S₀.1), _⟩ is a measurable G(N,n)-valued map.
If all entries converge to those of T, then L^{ij}(x) = T_ij (Tendsto.limUnder_eq), so M(x) = T.1 ∈ 𝒢, x ∈ Y and τ(x) = T (Subtype.ext).

audit.reason: The statement correctly includes an arbitrary measurable domain, measurable entries, and nonemptiness for the fallback plane. Countability and completeness justify measurable convergence sets and limUnder. Matrix.of, the closed projection predicate, and the measurable piecewise subtype construction use the intended instances. Entrywise limit identification and Subtype.ext establish the exact pointwise property. All seven proof steps are sufficient and non-circular.

subproblem.title: The closed-ball mass x ↦ μ(B_r(x)) of an s-finite measure on ℝ^N is Borel
subproblem.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, let ℝ^N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) carry its Borel σ-algebra, and let μ be an s-finite measure on ℝ^N. Then for every r ∈ ℝ the map ℝ^N → [0, ∞], x ↦ μ(B_r(x)), is Borel measurable, where B_r(x) = closedBall x r = {y : dist y x ≤ r} is the closed ball (empty when r < 0).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)), SFinite μ → ∀ r : ℝ, Measurable (fun x : Euclidean N ↦ μ (closedBall x r))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 2 of the parent-supplied proof of frt_vgm_measurable_plane_selection (part of the Borel version of x ↦ T_x needed in Simon, Ch. 8, proof of 1.2, p. 208). There it is applied to μ = μ_V = V.weight, which is σ-finite (Varifold.weight.instSigmaFinite) and hence s-finite; here it is stated for an arbitrary s-finite μ.

Library note: SimonGMT's Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.measurable_closedBall_mass_of_sFinite (Chapter01/InfiniteDensitySet.lean:29) proves the same fact on metric spaces, but it uses a file-local `borel X` instance and its file is not imported by GMT.Ch08.Submission (Lean reports Unknown identifier). The argument below is therefore given directly; it compiles in the pinned environment.

Let N ∈ ℕ, let μ be an s-finite measure on ℝ^N and let r ∈ ℝ.

1. Let D_r := {p ∈ ℝ^N × ℝ^N : dist p.2 p.1 ≤ r}. The map p ↦ dist p.2 p.1 is continuous on ℝ^N × ℝ^N (Continuous.dist of continuous_snd and continuous_fst), so D_r is closed (isClosed_le with the constant r).

2. ℝ^N is second countable with its Borel σ-algebra, so the product σ-algebra on ℝ^N × ℝ^N contains every open set (OpensMeasurableSpace of the product, available because the factors are second countable). Hence the closed set D_r is measurable (IsClosed.measurableSet).

3. For every x ∈ ℝ^N, the slice of D_r at x is the closed ball: Prod.mk x ⁻¹' D_r = {y : dist y x ≤ r} = closedBall x r (Metric.mem_closedBall; extensionality in y).

4. Because μ is s-finite and D_r is measurable, measurable_measure_prodMk_left (with ν := μ and s := D_r) shows that x ↦ μ(Prod.mk x ⁻¹' D_r) is measurable.

5. Rewriting each slice with Step 3 turns this function into x ↦ μ(closedBall x r), which is therefore measurable. No assumption on the sign of r is used (for r < 0 every slice is empty and the function is constantly 0). ∎
proof_key_steps: D_r = {(x, y) : dist y x ≤ r} is closed in ℝ^N × ℝ^N, hence measurable (second-countable factors).
The slice Prod.mk x ⁻¹' D_r equals closedBall x r for every x.
μ is s-finite, so measurable_measure_prodMk_left makes x ↦ μ(Prod.mk x ⁻¹' D_r) measurable.
Rewrite the slices to get measurability of x ↦ μ(closedBall x r).

audit.reason: The prose and exact type include arbitrary dimension, an s-finite measure, and every real radius. The closed incidence set is measurable in the product Borel space; its slices are exactly the closed balls. measurable_measure_prodMk_left applies with precisely the supplied s-finiteness hypothesis. The complete argument also covers negative radii and uses neither siblings nor the parent.
